meta_desc: Motion Adventure — GCSE Physics basics: speed, velocity, acceleration, distance, displacement, and units.
final_note: You learned the vocab of motion — speed vs velocity, distance vs displacement, and what acceleration really means.

concepts.def: How fast something moves, in m/s — no direction
Speed in a stated direction — a vector
Total path length travelled, in metres
Straight-line distance from start, with direction
Rate of change of velocity, in m/s²
A quantity with size only — no direction

walkthroughs.body_html:
Speed tells you how fast. Velocity tells you how fast and which way.

A car at 30 m/s has a speed. A car at 30 m/s north has a velocity.

Both are measured in metres per second (m/s).

Distance is the total path you travel. Displacement is how far you end up from the start, in a straight line.

Walk 3 m east then 3 m back west: distance is 6 m, but displacement is 0 m. 🚶

Distance is a scalar. Displacement is a vector — it has direction.

Acceleration is how quickly velocity changes. Units: m/s².

If a car speeds up from 0 to 20 m/s in 5 seconds, its acceleration is 20 ÷ 5 = 4 m/s².

Slowing down is just negative acceleration — sometimes called deceleration.
